chunks: From him, from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, from Ẓarīf — meaning Ibn Nāṣiḥ — from Thaʿlabah ibn Maymūn, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Yazīd, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
There is no wudu (ablution) required because of pumpkin seeds and small worms; they are only like lice.

key_terms.بِمَنْزِلَةِ: in the status or category of
key_terms.وُضُوءٌ: wudu (ablution), ritual washing required for certain acts of worship

ai.seo_question: Does encountering small worms or similar tiny creatures require wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling that contact with pumpkin seeds and small worms does not necessitate wudu (ablution). The Imam عليه السلام compares them to lice, indicating that such things do not invalidate ritual purity.
